Description: Includes the 73m victory minaret, Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, and iron pillar. Citations: J.A. Page (1926), 'An Historical Memoir on the Qutb: Delhi (ASI)'; Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'.

Square sandstone mausoleum with Arabic calligraphy and geometric carvings. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

India's earliest Islamic mausoleum, built as an underground crypt for Prince Nasiruddin Mahmud. Citations: S.A.A. Rizvi (1987), 'The Wonder That Was India Vol. II'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

Historical ruin containing the earliest true arch and dome in Indian Islamic architecture. Citations: Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.
